newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma winter wheat seeding nearly completed.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma winter wheat seeding nearly completed.

text.p: Planting of Oklahoma's winter wheat crop neared completion during the week ended Sunday, according to the Oklahoma Agricultural Statistics Service weekly state crop report.

Planting and harvesting was slowed in many areas by wet fields at the beginning of the week, with activities increasing as fields dried out during the week. Soybean and peanut harvest were past the halfway point.
Some areas reported washing of small grains fields as a result of heavy weekend rains.
Wheat planted 94 percent vs 90 week ago, 91 year ago, 92 on a five-year average. Wheat was 72 percent emerged versus 57 percent a week earlier, 52 a year ago and 67 percent average.
Wheat rated 75 percent good to excellent, up from 78 at that level last week.
Sorghum was 29 percent harvested versus 20 a week earlier, 29 a year ago and 34 percent average. Sorghum was rated 92 good to excellent, versus 91 last week.

Soybeans harvested stood at 55 percent versus 53 a week earlier, 46 a year ago and 44 percent average. Eighty-nine percent were mature versus 84 percent a week earlier, 68 a year ago and 79 percent average.
Soybeans were rated 63 percent good to excellent versus 66 the previous week.
Cotton bolls were 79 percent opened versus 71 a week earlier, 63 a year earlier and 80 percent average. Cotton was 19 percent harvested versus 10 a week earlier, nine a year earlier and 26 average.
Cotton was rated 33 good/excellent, up from 26 last week.
Pasture and range condition rated 77 percent good to excellent versus 76 last week.
